account:
Something unusually coordinated seems to be happening around the great hall today. The baker and innkeeper were at town hall unusually early. The baker spoke of two hundred jubilee loaves, and the innkeeper said this was his private commission and responsibility to pay, not town business. I overheard freight say he had placed 160 loaves in the hall table chest at minus fifty, thirty, while the baker said he delivered thirty-two separately and that his bakery bread chest was empty. Those reported deliveries total 192, so I have not confirmed delivery of the full two hundred. The baker also asked the innkeeper to settle the account and repay a promised thirty emeralds.

The innkeeper has repeatedly mentioned my eighteen-hundred lighting inspection. That inspection with the builder was added yesterday with my authorization, and the secretary is supposed to bring me into the hall. The combination of jubilee bread, private funding, hall storage, and an arranged evening visit makes me suspect preparations for a celebration, possibly a surprise meant to include me. I do not know its actual purpose or whether anyone is deliberately keeping it from me. The secretary is involved in my appointments and grain enquiries; that alone does not establish involvement in any surprise.

Townsfolk have also repeated oddly vague news about a bridge or port change at the bakery, mentioning the baker and neighbour and a sack of bread. I have not seen any such change or obtained a clear explanation, so I cannot tell whether this concerns transport, building work, or merely confused reports.

I am keeping my appointments. At this morning's mill inspection, the secretary and I confirmed a posted price of two emeralds per hay bale and observed seventy-three bales in the stall chest, equivalent to 657 wheat. We do not know how much is already committed, who manages the supply, where the miller is, or the delivery terms. Freight previously arranged wheat for the baker's private order. No town purchase has been authorized. We intend to ask the baker about the supplier, while preserving my noon lunch and later appointments.
